speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; you are here for right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning after a rear-end collision, correct? To begin, can you describe exactly how the leg was positioned when the injury occurred and how severe the pain is on a scale of 1 to 10?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; please describe precisely how your right leg is currently positioned compared to your left, and does it feel unstable or give way when you try to bear weight? Additionally, did you experience any clicking or popping sounds in the right hip or knee at the moment of impact?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Femoral Neck Fracture. The clinical presentation of a shortened, externally rotated (note: patient reported internal rotation, which can occur with specific fracture patterns or muscle spasm), and adducted leg following high-energy trauma is classic for this injury. Immediate orthopedic consultation and radiographic imaging are required.
